name: United States
maturity_rationale: Assessment: alliance-level integration across SATCOM (WGS), SDA hosting (C-band, SST, DARC), operations (Olympic Defender) and command-level instruments (ESC MOU 2023, SoI June 2026).
one_line: Australia's principal space ally; provides core SATCOM and SDA architecture and has opened its Force Design process to allies.
evidence_ids: EV-USSFCSPO-11; EV-USSFCSPO-12; EV-USSFCSPO-15; EV-USSFCSPO-16; EV-USSFCSPO-17; EV-USSFCSPO-18; EV-AUINPUTS-13

name: United Kingdom
maturity_rationale: Assessment: DARC trilateral partner and AUKUS export-control counterpart; fewer dedicated bilateral space instruments evidenced than for the US.
one_line: DARC trilateral partner and AUKUS licence-free trade counterpart with an updated Space Bridge arrangement.

name: Japan
maturity_rationale: Assessment: treaty-level RAA, shared CSpO membership and deep civil space interdependence (Himawari, QZSS, ALOS); defence-space lines of effort not yet explicit in FSDC-era statements.
one_line: Closest Indo-Pacific partner with operational civil space interdependence and a maturing military space organisation.
evidence_ids: EV-JAPANAU-01; EV-JAPANAU-10; EV-JAPANAU-13; EV-JAPANAU-14; EV-JAPANAU-15; EV-CONVERSA-03

name: India
maturity_rationale: Assessment: leader-level 2026 Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation and proven civil space delivery (Cocos TT&C, crew-recovery agreement); no defence-space instrument yet.
one_line: Rapidly deepening strategic partner whose Gaganyaan support already monetises Australian Indian Ocean geography.

name: Germany
maturity_rationale: Assessment: CSpO co-member with strong national SDA assets and commercial launch activity in South Australia, but no dedicated bilateral government-to-government space instrument identified (EV-GERMANY-21).
one_line: Capable European space actor that names Australia an attractive partner but engages mainly through CSpO and commercial channels.

name: United Arab Emirates
maturity_rationale: Assessment: 2019 agency-level MoU is civil-only and expressly non-binding; shared Artemis Accords founding membership; no defence dimension evidenced (EV-UAE-21).
one_line: Well-funded, mission-driven space actor newly bound tighter into the US technology-security perimeter (EAR Country Group A:5, July 2026).

name: Pacific Islands Forum
maturity_rationale: Assessment: policy-level engagement through the Boe Declaration and 2050 Strategy; no space-specific regional mechanism evidenced.
one_line: Regional body whose endorsed security and connectivity frameworks give Australia a Pacific-defined pathway for space-enabled assistance.

name: New Zealand
maturity_rationale: Assessment: alliance-grade general defence relationship - both governments use 'alliance' language in their own top-level strategy (EV-NZ-01, EV-NZ-02) - but near-zero space-specific track. No bilateral space instrument was located (EV-NZ-17); the 2018 CDR statement and the March 2026 ANZMIN 2+2 contain no space content (EV-NZ-04, EV-NZ-05); the only shared space vehicle is multilateral CSpO (EV-NZ-15). Scored level with Germany (2) on space specificity, not on relationship depth.
one_line: Australia's closest defence partner and treaty ally with a genuine launch industry, yet no bilateral space instrument and no space line of effort in any bilateral ministerial statement.
evidence_ids: EV-NZ-01; EV-NZ-02; EV-NZ-03; EV-NZ-04; EV-NZ-05; EV-NZ-06; EV-NZ-15; EV-NZ-17

name: Quad (Australia-India-Japan-US)
maturity_rationale: Assessment: active space working group and summit-level commitments since 2021, but all documented commitments are civil-domain only (EV-QUADINDI-23).
one_line: Civil-domain space cooperation vehicle (EO data gateway, civil SSA expertise sharing, Indo-Pacific capacity building).

name: AUKUS (Australia-UK-US)
maturity_rationale: Assessment: operative licence-free export environment (finalised Dec 2025) and DARC delivery in train; MTCR launch-vehicle technology remains excluded.
one_line: Delivery and export-control framework: DARC under a trilateral MoU plus the ITAR/EAR/DTC licence-free environment.

name: Combined Space Operations Initiative
region: Ten-nation (AU, CA, FR, DE, IT, JP, NZ, NO, UK, US)
maturity_rationale: Assessment: Australia a participant since the 2014 start and CSpO Vision 2031 co-releaser; active Principals' Board (April 2026) with MNF-OOD focus; instruments non-binding.
one_line: The principal multilateral military space forum linking Australia to nine partners, now prioritising Operation Olympic Defender.
